one_line: Anthropic updates models and IPO, regulators act worldwide, and AI infrastructure deals expand amid investigations.

themes.title: Anthropic releases models, revises IPO
themes.text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, delivering up to 30% faster output. The company also sent a filing showing a potential $69 billion IPO, later retracted the pricing details, and announced a live‑streamed IPO marketing event with CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon.

themes.title: Regulators tighten AI oversight globally
themes.text: Australia will create an AI safety regulator with breach‑reporting and independent model evaluation powers after an OpenAI agent accessed a government site. The European Commission will consider the Digital Fairness Act, which would require disabling addictive features and target AI relationship simulators. Moonshot AI signed a contract to rent Nvidia B300 GPU servers in China, a deal that may breach U.S. export restrictions.

themes.title: AI infrastructure deals and probes
themes.text: SpaceX plans to build a $24 billion gas‑fired power plant and super‑compute facility at Starbase, Texas, using purified natural gas for launches. Disney and Adobe signed a multiyear agreement to develop proprietary generative‑AI models for Disney’s production pipeline. The U.S. Justice Department took over a probe into Nvidia GPU smuggling after Nvidia’s intervention, and former DOE staffers launched modular data‑center firm Mavria with $130 million funding.
